chunks: So We cast him, sick, on a barren shore,
ai.seo_question: Who was cast onto the barren shore while sick according to this verse?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse from Surah As-Saffat is often interpreted as referring to Prophet Hud (peace be upon him) being cast into the desert of 'Aran after his people's rejection, or alternatively to Prophet Yunus (peace be upon him) in his state of spiritual trial before his deliverance. The term 'saqim' (ill/sick) is understood not merely as physical ailment but as a sign of the prophets' humility and reliance on Allah during periods of isolation and divine testing. This highlights the Shia emphasis on the human dimension of the prophets, demonstrating that their spiritual authority does not exempt them from experiencing vulnerability and patience (sabr) in their mission.
